records.deidentified_narrative: on tuesday the 15th day of october, 2024 i, corporal j. crabb #458 was assigned to the comal county sheriffs office (ccso) traffic safety and enforcement unit. police responded to [roadway]. new braunfels, comal county, texas (brauntex quarry) for a report of a truck tractor semi trailer combination having struck a worker that was on foot. while en route to this location, dispatch advised the female appeared awake but was non-responsive. the female was identified as jennifer bader w/f [date]. upon my arrival it was dark outside with no apparent natural lighting and this area was only dimly lit at times by artificial lighting such as headlamps with a consistent artificial lighting from the tail lamps of a truck on the property. this portion of the property was mostly dirt and rock with a large section of pavement on the northwest portion of the property running from the back of the property to the entrance/exit at [roadway]. i was informed this roadway is used for trucks to utilize a wash out on the property. i observed a female on the paved portion of the roadway laying on the ground and being attended to by new braunfels fire and ems. i observed the female was not wearing a helmet or a reflective vest. deputy hernandez #347 was on scene speaking to witnesses who advised the female was hit by the rear portion of semi trailer and it was unknown whether the trailer ran her over or just struck her. the witness advised jennifer had exited a large dump truck on the quarry property and exited the truck to speak to a driver identified as gerleydis lobaina rodriguez h/m [date]. . at some point during this conversation with lobaina, jennifer stepped backwards onto the paved section of the roadway as a truck tractor semi trailer was driving by. jennifer reportedly stepped backwards either onto or towards the paved roadway after the truck tractor portion of the combination had passed. it was reported that the rear passenger side fender well portion of the trailer struck jennifer on the right side causing her to fall. lobaina provided dash cam evidence of this incident. in the dash cam video jennifer can be seen walking in front of lobainas truck with no helmet and no vest. jennifer appears to approach lobainas drivers side door before exiting the camera field of view. at 1:06 in the dash cam video a truck passes. at 2:56 lobaina enters the frame appearing to be seeking help from other employees at the plant. it should be noted that no other vehicles pass at this time. this truck tractor semi trailer was identified as a freightliner [identifier] bearing txlp: 1m81411 hauling an unloaded armorlite commercial belly dump trailer bearing oklp: [identifier]. this vehicle was identified based on numerous distinguish characters such as the lettering on the passenger door and its relation to the window on the door, a single stack exhaust pipe on the passenger side with the heat shield, the front passenger side bumper with damage folding it inwards towards the cab, the paint scheme of the cab and front left fender, the size and shape of the windows as well as the lighting equipment. it should be noted the driver of this vehicle also provided information that he had gone to the wash out and returned to line which coincides with the direction of travel. there was no roadway evidence as the driver was unaware he had struck a pedestrian and did not brake. it should be noted that i did not locate any physical evidence on the truck or trailer which would not be uncommon for the vehicle having only struck a pedestrian in a specific spot. while on scene i also located a pair of glasses on the ground reported by brauntex employees to have belonged to jennifer. the glasses were intact other than the right temple tip portion leading to the ear was damaged and bent inwards. this crush evidence coincided with the witnesses initial statements and provided some point of impact. i spoke to the truck driver identified as daislan hernandez garcia [date] who advised he was unaware his trailer had struck jennifer but was otherwise cooperative. another male on scene assisted in translating spanish to english for us. the male assisted in translating but was not helpful with the investigative portion of this incident and began getting more argumentative than helpful and i ceased using his assistance. i directed deputy hernandez to bring the witnesses to this truck to further confirm this was the same vehicle. the involved males began talking to each other and then one of the original witnesses stated they did not see the trailer actually strike jennifer and that she may have fallen on her own, contradicting their original statements. i informed all involved parties at this time that a crash report would be generated regardless and for daislan to contact his company safety manager and their insurance. i then responded to [medical facility] in kyle, texas [medical facility], i observed jennifer had significant swelling on the right side of her head. i asked jennifer if she remembered what happened and jennifer stated she only remembered exiting her truck and could not recall the actual incident. i then looked at jennifers clothing. i observed jennifers jeans had been cut in several different spots to remove them for medical purposes. i did not observe any distinguishable markings or damage on jennifers boots. on jennifers shirt there was a spot on the upper left portion where the shirt had been stretched and worn down in one specific spot to a point it caused a large hole. the stretching, wear and ripping of the fibers is indicative of the clothing have been dragged along the pavement and stretched which along with the evidentiary crush on jennifers glasses, is indicative of her having been hit by an outside force causing her to hit the pavement with a level of force the shirt ripped and not jennifer simply falling. i provided all involved individuals with the [case id] for this incident. a crash report was also generated and completed. my in car and body worn camera were activated during this incident and are available if needed. no further action was taken by me at this time. eor.

records.public_safe_text: on tuesday the 15th day of october, 2024 i, corporal j. crabb #458 was assigned to the comal county sheriffs office (ccso) traffic safety and enforcement unit. police responded to [roadway]. new braunfels, comal county, texas (brauntex quarry) for a report of a truck tractor semi trailer combination having struck a worker that was on foot. while en route to this location, dispatch advised the female appeared awake but was non-responsive. the female was identified as jennifer bader w/f [date]. upon my arrival it was dark outside with no apparent natural lighting and this area was only dimly lit at times by artificial lighting such as headlamps with a consistent artificial lighting from the tail lamps of a truck on the property. this portion of the property was mostly dirt and rock with a large section of pavement on the northwest portion of the property running from the back of the property to the entrance/exit at [roadway]. i was informed this roadway is used for trucks to utilize a wash out on the property. i observed a female on the paved portion of the roadway laying on the ground and being attended to by new braunfels fire and ems. i observed the female was not wearing a helmet or a reflective vest. deputy hernandez #347 was on scene speaking to witnesses who advised the female was hit by the rear portion of semi trailer and it was unknown whether the trailer ran her over or just struck her. the witness advised jennifer had exited a large dump truck on the quarry property and exited the truck to speak to a driver identified as gerleydis lobaina rodriguez h/m [date]. . at some point during this conversation with lobaina, jennifer stepped backwards onto the paved section of the roadway as a truck tractor semi trailer was driving by. jennifer reportedly stepped backwards either onto or towards the paved roadway after the truck tractor portion of the combination had passed. it was reported that the rear passenger side fender well portion of the trailer struck jennifer on the right side causing her to fall. lobaina provided dash cam evidence of this incident. in the dash cam video jennifer can be seen walking in front of lobainas truck with no helmet and no vest. jennifer appears to approach lobainas drivers side door before exiting the camera field of view. at 1:06 in the dash cam video a truck passes. at 2:56 lobaina enters the frame appearing to be seeking help from other employees at the plant. it should be noted that no other vehicles pass at this time. this truck tractor semi trailer was identified as a freightliner [identifier] bearing txlp: 1m81411 hauling an unloaded armorlite commercial belly dump trailer bearing oklp: [identifier]. this vehicle was identified based on numerous distinguish characters such as the lettering on the passenger door and its relation to the window on the door, a single stack exhaust pipe on the passenger side with the heat shield, the front passenger side bumper with damage folding it inwards towards the cab, the paint scheme of the cab and front left fender, the size and shape of the windows as well as the lighting equipment. it should be noted the driver of this vehicle also provided information that he had gone to the wash out and returned to line which coincides with the direction of travel. there was no roadway evidence as the driver was unaware he had struck a pedestrian and did not brake. it should be noted that i did not locate any physical evidence on the truck or trailer which would not be uncommon for the vehicle having only struck a pedestrian in a specific spot. while on scene i also located a pair of glasses on the ground reported by brauntex employees to have belonged to jennifer. the glasses were intact other than the right temple tip portion leading to the ear was damaged and bent inwards. this crush evidence coincided with the witnesses initial statements and provided some point of impact. i spoke to the truck driver identified as daislan hernandez garcia [date] who advised he was unaware his trailer had struck jennifer but was otherwise cooperative. another male on scene assisted in translating spanish to english for us. the male assisted in translating but was not helpful with the investigative portion of this incident and began getting more argumentative than helpful and i ceased using his assistance. i directed deputy hernandez to bring the witnesses to this truck to further confirm this was the same vehicle. the involved males began talking to each other and then one of the original witnesses stated they did not see the trailer actually strike jennifer and that she may have fallen on her own, contradicting their original statements. i informed all involved parties at this time that a crash report would be generated regardless and for daislan to contact his company safety manager and their insurance. i then responded to [medical facility] in kyle, texas [medical facility], i observed jennifer had significant swelling on the right side of her head. i asked jennifer if she remembered what happened and jennifer stated she only remembered exiting her truck and could not recall the actual incident. i then looked at jennifers clothing. i observed jennifers jeans had been cut in several different spots to remove them for medical purposes. i did not observe any distinguishable markings or damage on jennifers boots. on jennifers shirt there was a spot on the upper left portion where the shirt had been stretched and worn down in one specific spot to a point it caused a large hole. the stretching, wear and ripping of the fibers is indicative of the clothing have been dragged along the pavement and stretched which along with the evidentiary crush on jennifers glasses, is indicative of her having been hit by an outside force causing her to hit the pavement with a level of force the shirt ripped and not jennifer simply falling. i provided all involved individuals with the [case id] for this incident. a crash report was also generated and completed. my in car and body worn camera were activated during this incident and are available if needed. no further action was taken by me at this time. eor.
